Un total de 17 vuelos de llegada y salida del Aeropuerto Internacional Luis Muñoz Marín, en Carolina, resultaron afectados este viernes por las condiciones climatológicas en la costa noreste de Estados Unidos, según informó Aerostar Airport Holdings.

El informe de operaciones irregulares, divulgado a las 9:45 a.m. de este viernes, detalla nueve vuelos cancelados y otros ocho con retrasos.

En el caso de las llegadas, se reportaron cinco cancelaciones y seis retrasos, con un estimado de 1,849 pasajeros afectados. Los vuelos procedían de ciudades como Nueva York, Newark, Boston, Hartford y Filadelfia.

Mientras, entre las salidas se registraron cuatro cancelaciones y dos retrasos, que podrían afectar a unos 904 pasajeros. Los destinos incluidos en el informe fueron Nueva York y Hartford.

Las aerolíneas con vuelos impactados fueron JetBlue, United, Frontier, Avelo y Delta. Aerostar atribuyó todas las interrupciones a las condiciones del tiempo en el noreste de Estados Unidos.

En total, la compañía estimó que 2,753 pasajeros podrían verse afectados por las cancelaciones y los retrasos.

Two hours had passed since Sam's Club's midnight opening, but people continued to enter the store, and dozens of families lined up to pay. This was attributed to their choice of campaign coinciding with the start of Buen Fin rather than El Fin Irresistible. In an interview with MILENIO, Sergio Pérez, Marketing Director of Sam's Club in Mexico, explained that this strategy was designed to allow consumers to compare prices from El Fin Irresistible, which starts at least a week earlier, helping them make purchasing decisions in the initial moments of Buen Fin. According to the Mexican Association of Online Sales (AMVO), 67 percent of Mexicans take between one to four weeks to compare prices.

"Today we welcome Buen Fin, but we start earlier with El Fin Irresistible; we do this because we love giving our members the opportunity to compare and make the best decision regarding the products they want to buy," he explained. . . Last year, Walmart de México y Centroamérica decided to participate in Buen Fin again after a six-year absence, having distanced itself from the National Association of Self-Service and Department Stores (Antad) for the 15th anniversary in 2025. Although in its fourth-quarter report for 2025, the company noted that its return to Buen Fin "did not meet initial expectations," over 76 million transactions were recorded in stores and clubs, along with more than 180 million visits to its e-commerce platform. Therefore, Pérez added that starting their midnight opening with this campaign would become a tradition for the company. . . "It was spectacular; there were a lot of people, and our members were very happy... we made the decision to open at a different club, and we slightly adjusted the date because we wanted to support the entire Buen Fin strategy and give our members the opportunity to compare," he stated. . . Sam's strategy for this opening goes beyond just the timing. The executive indicated that they anticipated a higher number of customers due to specific promotions and products integrated into the campaign, including appliances, technology, and furniture. They also set up experience zones. . . "We have focused on designing a strategy that meets all our members' needs, giving them the chance to listen, feel, and try the products. So, yes, we expected this response from the people; we prepared extensively for this and dedicated significant time to understanding our members," he said.

On the morning of November 13, Sam's Club also unveiled its new image, aligned with changes made in the United States to foster a sense of belonging among its members. . . "Everything revolves around the community... in the community we create based on this sense of belonging, where we are an inclusive club for everyone... we needed this. We used what they did in the United States as a foundation; it was an 18-month project for this redesign, and we decided to bring it to Mexico," he added. . . According to Walmart's latest quarterly report, the company's same-store sales grew by 1.7 percent year-over-year, led by Sam's Club.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Rodrigo García Jaques, CEO of Spin, raised the possibility that Oxxo and Fomento Económico Mexicano (FEMSA) could establish their own bank in the future, asserting that the transition of the financial platform into a banking institution has not been forgotten but is merely on hold.

During his participation in the panel "The Art of Business Reinvention" at the EL CEO Forum, the executive noted that as things progress and improve, they will eventually seek a banking license.

The license is not forgotten; it is frozen," stated the CEO of Spin.

He also mentioned that they will take the necessary time, whether it takes one, two, three, or four years, to offer consumers the products they need; this process will likely involve significant experimentation.

In February 2025, FEMSA revealed its intentions to take Spin to the next level and seek a banking license. Juan Carlos Guillermety, then CEO of Spin, explained that there were plans to expand their financial offerings, which included incorporating payroll and credit services.

By October of the same year, FEMSA's Chief Financial Officer, Martín Arias, reported that the company preferred to first strengthen its credit business and better understand its capacity to utilize customer data before requesting the license.

However, FEMSA confirmed that it would delay the banking application until it had greater visibility over the results of its credit opportunities. Thus, operational strengthening of Oxxo in the country and the consolidation of Spin within its commercial ecosystem were prioritized.

What is Spin?

FEMSA identified the financial business as an opportunity to diversify its operations beyond convenience stores. This led to the creation of Spin by Oxxo, a digital platform that began operations in Mexico in March 2021, aiming to facilitate payments and bring financial services closer to its consumers.

In its early years, the app focused on offering money transfers, deposits, withdrawals, utility payments, and purchases using a Visa card, leveraging Oxxo's infrastructure to connect cash with digital services.

The project took a significant step forward in October 2022 when the National Banking and Securities Commission (CNBV) authorized Compropago, the company operating the Spin brand, to operate as an Electronic Payment Fund Institution (IFPE). This strengthened its presence in the Mexican financial sector.

Its growth was rapid: in April 2023, it reached six million customers, and a year later, it surpassed ten million.

Over time, FEMSA expanded its focus to include new services, such as remittances, payment solutions for businesses, and credit alternatives. Thus, Spin evolved from being a digital wallet linked to consumption at Oxxo to becoming one of the conglomerate's key initiatives to compete in the digital financial ecosystem.

Investing in innovation is essential for growth

During his participation in the same panel at the EL CEO Forum, executives from Natura, Unilever, Phillip Morris, and Spin agreed that investment in research and development for innovation is necessary.

David Cabrera, Vice President of Sales at Unilever Mexico, noted that consumer preferences are changing and will continue to do so. He explained that their choices are no longer limited to product purchases but also include experiences such as concerts and sporting events, prompting companies to invest in technology to enhance their products for the benefit of customers.

Manuel Chinchilla, CEO of Phillips Morris, indicated that they have focused on investing in research and development to move away from traditional smoking, thus achieving consumer acceptance and maintaining their commitment to them.

Francisco Demesa, CEO of Natura & Avon Mexico, stated that while the company emphasizes an omnichannel approach, it does not neglect what they refer to as relationship sales, as both modes complement each other to drive business growth.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Argosy Investors has recently highlighted Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FMX) as a key holding in its Q1 2026 investor letter. The letter, made available on June 8th, 2026, outlines a cautious approach toward investment amid a transformative landscape characterized by an AI capital expenditure boom.

In the letter, Argosy expressed skepticism regarding the sustainability of earnings for market participants and suppliers during this capex surge. The firm emphasized the challenge of balancing supply and demand, especially given the rapid advancement of AI technologies. As companies experience rising volumes and prices, there is a growing concern that earnings could be overstated if supply ramps up faster than anticipated. Despite these concerns, Argosy has identified Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. as a viable investment option.

Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., a prominent global franchise bottler of Coca-Cola beverages, closed at $122.88 per share on June 5th, 2026. The company's stock has seen a modest decline of 0.19% over the past month, though it enjoyed a robust gain of 17.29% over the past year. With a market capitalization of $41.86 billion, Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. remains a significant player in the beverage industry.

Argosy Investors revealed its strategic move of selling shares in Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) to reallocate funds into Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. The firm expressed confidence in FMX's exposure to Coca-Cola, noting the synergistic benefits of expanding convenience store operations alongside increasing beverage sales in Mexico. This pivot underscores Argosy's belief in the growth potential of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. in a rapidly evolving market.

While Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. is not currently among the most popular stocks held by hedge funds, it still garners attention. Argosy Investors remains optimistic about FMX, even as it acknowledges that certain AI stocks may present greater upside potential and lower downside risk.

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

6.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

4.1 Activities

Grupo Financiero Banorte, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading financial institution in Mexico, offering a comprehensive range of services including retail and commercial banking, insurance, investment banking, and asset management. As one of the country's largest banks by assets, it serves individuals, businesses, and institutions through a vast network of branches and digital platforms. The company's core activities focus on providing accessible financial solutions such as loans, deposits, credit cards, and wealth management, emphasizing innovation and customer-centric strategies. In recent years, Banorte has seen fastest-growing segments in digital banking and fintech solutions, which have expanded its online services and mobile app usage, as well as in lending to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), fueled by economic recovery and technological advancements. This growth has strengthened its market position, enabling it to adapt to evolving consumer needs while maintaining robust risk management practices. It is Mexico's 3rd largest Bank by market capitalization.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Jun 15, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA's Returnable Glass Bottle: A Timeless Choice for Latin American Consumers

Coca-Cola FEMSA's standardized returnable glass bottle remains a core workhorse in Latin America, combining refillable packaging with industrial-scale distribution. As of 15th June 2026, the bottle continues to play a vital role, particularly in Mexico and Brazil, where refillable containers are a staple of consumer habits.

The Coca-Cola returnable glass bottle is typically available in familiar single-serve formats ranging from 235 ml to 355 ml, as well as larger family sizes such as 1.0 liter and 1.25 liters. These offerings are tailored to local preferences, making them more appealing to consumers in different markets. Beyond its nostalgic appeal, the refillable glass format serves a practical purpose in Coca-Cola FEMSA's packaging mix, providing a robust container that can endure multiple wash-and-refill cycles on industrial bottling lines.

The returnable glass bottle operates on a deposit-return system, where consumers pay a deposit upon purchase and reclaim it when they return the empty bottle. This model encourages recycling and reinforces Coca-Cola FEMSA's commitment to sustainability. In the markets where Coca-Cola FEMSA operates, these bottles are commonly found in traditional trade outlets, including neighborhood stores, small groceries, and food-service channels, coexisting alongside one-way PET bottles and cans.

For Coca-Cola FEMSA, the returnable glass bottle is not merely a product but a strategic asset that caters to price-sensitive consumers while enhancing the company's sustainability narrative around refillable packaging. As of 13th June 2026, shares of Coca-Cola FEMSA (US1912411089) were trading at $105.08 on the NYSE, reflecting investor confidence in the company's enduring packaging strategies.

Over the years, Coca-Cola FEMSA has adapted its returnable glass bottle to meet evolving consumer needs and preferences. With a longstanding presence in the market, this packaging format continues to resonate with everyday soft-drink consumers in Latin America, particularly among price-conscious households and small food-service operators. The combination of tradition and practicality ensures that Coca-Cola FEMSA's returnable glass bottle remains a relevant and cherished choice.

May 19, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Amplifies Market Presence with Strategic Investments

Mexico City, May 19, 2026. Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest bottler by sales volume of the Coca-Cola System, continues to strengthen its leadership in Latin America through strategic investments that expand its production capacity, modernize its infrastructure, and strengthen its operating platform in the region. By optimizing production processes and modernizing facilities, the company aims to create a robust operating model that is both future-proof and aligned with market demands. This commitment to operational excellence is crucial as Coca-Cola FEMSA navigates the dynamic beverage landscape in Latin America.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. 5.1 Activities

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Director

Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez

Independent Director

Mr. Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. In addition, he has been Commissioner and Member of the Board of Directors of various companies within the industrial, commercial and financial sectors. He holds a degree in Public Accounting from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, a diploma in Financial Engineering from Colegio de Contadores Publicos de Mexico and a diploma in High Management from Universidad Iberoamericana.

He graduated in Public Accounting from Universidad Anahuac.

Frantz Joseph Guns Devos

Independent Director

Mr. Frantz Joseph Guns Devos serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He has worked at Aeropuertos del Sureste, Infraestructura Portuaria Mexicana and Ferrocarriles del Sureste.
